title: EFC — Mathematical Framework for Energy Flow in Space-Time
description: Introduces Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) as a theoretical framework where an energy-flow vector field interacts with entropy and standard relativistic boundary conditions to shape space-time dynamics. The work proposes integrating energy-flow effects into Einstein’s field equations and outlines qualitative predictions for cosmic expansion in low-density regions, black hole horizon stability, and temporal coherence of quantum fluctuations.

key_results.main_finding: Proposes a theoretical EFC framework where an energy-flow vector field coupled to entropy modifies space-time dynamics and yields qualitative predictions for cosmic void acceleration, black hole horizon stability, and quantum-scale temporal coherence.

sealed_predictions.statement: Low-density cosmic regions (voids) exhibit enhanced acceleration due to redistribution of energy by the energy-flow field.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Environmental dependence tests of the Hubble residuals and growth in/around voids (e.g., SN Ia Hubble diagram vs. density, void Alcock–Paczynski, BAO-in-voids, weak-lensing profiles) showing no extra acceleration beyond ΛCDM.

sealed_predictions.statement: Energy flow contributes to sustaining and shaping event-horizon dynamics and stability in black holes.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Precision tests of black hole ringdown spectra (quasi-normal mode frequencies/damping) and EHT horizon-scale observables finding complete consistency with GR without any additional terms attributable to energy-flow effects.

sealed_predictions.statement: Energy flow provides a mechanism for temporal coherence at microscopic (quantum) scales.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-sensitivity laboratory interferometry and quantum noise spectroscopy detecting no anomalous temporal coherence or correlations beyond standard quantum predictions once EFC’s coupling is quantitatively specified.

kill_criteria: KC1: Observations of expansion and growth in cosmic voids (SN Ia, BAO-in-voids, AP tests, weak lensing) show no additional acceleration or redistribution signature beyond ΛCDM within uncertainties tight enough to exclude EFC’s predicted effect.

KC2: Black hole ringdown measurements (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA/LISA) and horizon-scale imaging (EHT, next-gen EHT) are fully described by GR with no detectable deviations that could be attributed to an energy-flow contribution to horizon stability.

KC3: Precision laboratory and cosmological probes of quantum temporal coherence find no anomalies attributable to energy-flow coupling across the sensitivity range that EFC specifies once quantitatively formulated.

KC4: Any consistent formulation of the EFC-modified field equations demonstrably violates local energy–momentum conservation or causality under the stated boundary condition that c is the limiting speed, or fails basic consistency checks (well-posedness, stability) in realistic spacetimes.
